body:
maya: Hey all — kicking off a short thread to align on the new runtime dashboards and the alert -> pager mapping. We need a clear playbook before rollout next week. TL;DR: what metrics drive paging, thresholds, and which team gets paged for burn-rate vs infra saturation?

chris: +1. I sketched a first pass in the console mock. High level: latency SLO burn (p95 delta), error-rate spike, and queue/backlog depth. Separate alerts for capacity (runtime) vs correctness (model/infra).

leo: Agree. For oncall routing: infra/runtime ops should get capacity pages (GPU saturation, queue depth). Platform should get SLO burn/regression pages (p95 drift, request errors). We need cooldowns to avoid noisy burn-rate pages.

sam: Can we be explicit about thresholds and use-case examples? e.g., p95 increases by >30% over 1h AND errors >0.5% -> platform page. If only node-level GPU util >92% -> runtime page.

pat: Note: some customers will be on Dedicated where autoscaling isnt immediate. For Dedicated pool overload, page the account-owner team + eng-runtime. We should include a routing tag on the metric for "deployment_type" so rules can bifurcate.

chris: I'll draft concrete Prometheus-style rules. Example rule for SLO burn:
```
alert: SLOBurnRateHigh
expr: (sum(rate(requests_slo_burn[1h])) by (service) / sum(rate(requests_total[1h])) by (service)) > 0.3
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: critical
annotations:
  summary: "{{ $labels.service }} SLO burn >30% over 1h"
```
This would map to the "platform-slo" pager policy. Thoughts?

maya: That looks reasonable. 15m for sustained burn makes sense to avoid transient noise. Also add an eval window for canary rollouts (we should not page for canary <5% traffic unless burn >50%).

leo: For capacity alerts, keep shorter for immediate ops response: e.g., queue_length > 1000 for 5m OR GPU_utilization > 90% for 2m -> route to eng-runtime with high severity. Also attach the shard/pool label so oncall can triage region/pool quickly.

sam: Regarding pager policies: platform-slo -> pages Platform on-call. runtime-capacity -> pages Runtime on-call. For cross-cutting issues (both peaked and errors), page both but with primary/secondary roles. We should also include an escalation path: after 10m if no ack escalate to Platform Lead.

maya: Are we using existing PagerDuty services? We should map labels -> PD service in the alert manager config. @deploy-bot can you post the current mapping?

deploy-bot: Current mapping:
- "platform-slo" -> PD service: redwood-platform-prod
- "runtime-capacity" -> PD service: redwood-runtime-prod
- "dedicated-account" -> PD service: redwood-dedicated-ops
(see internal docs: https://go/redwood/alerting-mapping)

pat: One more nuance: quantization/precision regressions often surface as higher token cost or increased p99 latency for embeddings. Should we add a cost-anomaly alert that pages ML infra + Platform? Example: token_cost_per_request change >40% over 24h.

chris: Yep. Draft rule:
```
alert: TokenCostAnomaly
expr: (increase(token_cost_sum[24h]) / increase(requests_total[24h])) > 1.4 * avg_over_time((increase(token_cost_sum[7d]) / increase(requests_total[7d]))[24h:])
for: 1h
```
Route to ml-infra + platform-sre.

leo: Also add SLO burn rate chart panels to the dashboard per-service with an embedded "runbook" link and a button to mute alerts for 30m for ongoing rollouts. That will reduce noisy interruptions during controlled experiments.

maya: Good call. UX asks: add a small rollout toggle that annotates dashboards (canary %) so oncall sees whether traffic matches expectations. We'll need a new telemetry label on requests: rollout_fraction.

sam: Action items then: 1) chris to post PR with concrete alert rules + labels. 2) leo to update PD mapping and add escalation timings. 3) pat to add deployment_type and rollout_fraction labels to request telemetry. 4) maya to update runbook sections and console UX for muting + rollout annotation. 5) ops sync to review on Thursday.

chris: I'll aim to open the PR by EOD today. I'll include examples and a short playbook snippet showing triage steps.

pat: If anyone needs a test cluster for firing synthetic alerts, ping me. I spun up a small staging pool.

maya: Thanks team. If no objections I'll schedule the ops sync and mark this doc as the canonical playbook for the rollout. :thumbsup:

chris: No objections from me.

leo: Fine from SRE side.

sam: 👍

deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC — alerting config merges during that time will be held until the window ends.
